pcs.pc_description: identify and verify the accompanying documents such as purchase orders, invoices, delivery challans, and material safety data sheets (MSDS) for incoming materials
check and match the details on the documentation with the actual material received including quantity, material code, batch number, and supplier information
ensure that all materials are labelled properly and match the specifications mentioned in the documentation and the purchase order
report any mismatch or missing documentation to the supervisor or relevant authority as per the organization’s standard operating procedure (SOP)
record the receipt of materials accurately in manual registers or digital inventory systems as instructed
segregate and place materials in the designated inspection area until quality checks are completed

follow the company’s procedures for handling, checking, and documentation of incoming materials in compliance with safety and quality guidelines
perform visual inspection of incoming materials for any physical damage, contamination, incorrect labeling, or packaging defects
identify surface defects such as cracks, discoloration, warping, or deformation using standard visual inspection methods
use appropriate measuring instruments like vernier calipers, measuring tapes, gauges, or scales to check dimensional accuracy of the materials
compare the measured dimensions with the specifications provided in the purchase order or technical drawing
ensure all inspection tools and instruments are calibrated and function correctly before use
document the inspection results in the inspection checklist or quality control register as per organizational protocol
report any non-conformity or deviations from quality standards to the department concerned or quality supervisor
follow standard procedures for accepting or rejecting materials based on inspection outcomes and escalate issues when required
identify deviations in materials from the required specifications, such as physical defects, incorrect quantity, or wrong type
tag and isolate non-conforming materials in a designated quarantine or rejection area to avoid mix-up with approved materials
document the details of non-conforming materials including supplier name, batch number, type of defect, and inspection outcome in the standard reporting format
notify the supervisor or quality assurance personnel regarding the discrepancies found during inspection
coordinate with the purchase or quality team for decisions related to rejection, replacement, or corrective actions for non-conforming materials
follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) for handling rejected goods as per company policy and safety guidelines
ensure accurate entry of non-conformance records in physical or digital systems for future traceability and audit purposes
support root cause analysis or supplier communication, if required, by providing detailed and timely reports on material discrepancies
